source.title: STARFlow: Scaling Latent Normalizing Flows for High-resolution Image Synthesis
source.authors: Jia-Tao Gu; Tian-Rong Chen; David Berthelot; Huangjie Zheng; Yu-Yang Wang; Rui-Xiang Zhang; Laurent Dinh; Miguel Angel Bautista; J. Susskind; Shuang-Fei Zhai

record.tranche_reason: The study examines image-model scaling, a different modality from the language-model scaling laws in the claim. It reports an NLL-versus-model-size sweep, but does not fit or state a power law.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Kaplan et al. for language-model scaling laws but does not test those laws directly. Its image-model scaling plots and the accompanying statement about deeper models are the relevant new results. Image-generation benchmark comparisons, decoder ablations, and guidance results do not test the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study cites Kaplan et al. but fits no power law. Its only scaling result is a deep-block depth sweep for image normalizing flows (Fig. 10c,d). The text says only that deeper models converge faster and end better. Monotone improvement with size, with no values, fit or exponent, cannot show whether loss follows a power law, so V5 (power-law form in other modalities) is not tested. The other versions concern language-model pretraining and are not studied.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that latent normalizing flows scale to high-resolution image and text-to-image generation, competitive with diffusion and autoregressive models, and that deeper models converge faster and perform better. They make no power-law scaling claim.
record.recipe_differences: Image-domain normalizing-flow scaling sweep; it does not reproduce language-model cross-entropy scaling or fit the original power laws.
record.method_sensitivity: Model size/deep-block depth and training progress are varied; the text reports faster convergence and better final performance for deeper models.

fits_no_version.finding: In STARFlow image normalizing flows, increasing deep-block depth gives faster convergence and lower final NLL and FID (no numbers or fit given).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Image normalizing-flow NLL decreases with model depth/size; functional form unspecified.

fits_no_version.finding: Allocating depth to one deep block matters more than the number of blocks. Deep-shallow allocation outperforms equal allocation (FID 4.69 vs 5.56 in pixel space), so shape matters for image flows.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In autoregressive image flows, how parameters are allocated across blocks substantially changes quality at a similar parameter count.

record.problems: The supplied text does not provide numerical values from the NLL-versus-size plot or state that its NLL is held out. It reports no power-law fit or uncertainty for the scaling results.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results were left out. The paper's other ablations and image-generation benchmarks do not measure the listed scaling-law versions.

untested.parts: Language-model pretraining loss vs. parameters, tokens or compute.
Extrapolation from small fits to larger runs.
Effect of architecture shape on language-model loss at a fixed parameter count.
Whether image-model loss follows a power-law form. The study reports only a qualitative depth sweep.
Downstream predictability from scale or loss.
Dependence of fitted exponents on setup and fitting choices.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's relation 'tests'/T3 for V5 is overruled. The paper is a method paper whose scaling sweep is qualitative, figure-only and unfitted. The architecture-allocation ablations (Fig. 10e,f; Table 1) concern image flows and FID, not language-model loss, so they do not bear on V4.

versions.untested_parts: Language-model held-out pretraining loss scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of much larger language-model runs from fits on smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its trend with compute.
Whether architecture details change loss only slightly at a fixed parameter count.
The study evaluates image-model NLL against model size, but does not report a power-law fit, its form or exponents, held-out status, or scaling across other modalities and training regimes.
Predictability of downstream-task performance from scale or pretraining loss.
Dependence of fitted scaling exponents or compute-optimal allocations on fitting and training choices, and departures from single power laws.

rows.subject: STARFlow
rows.size_stated: Model size varied; individual sizes not stated in the text accompanying the figure.
rows.operation_detail: Varied deep-block depth/model size and tracked negative log-likelihood over training.
rows.note: The text says deeper models converge faster and achieve better final performance, but does not say that the NLL follows a power law. The plotted values are not recoverable from the supplied text.
rows.check: NLL vs. deep-block depth for an image flow, shown in the figure only. No values, power-law fit or held-out status are stated, so the row cannot show V5's power-law form. The link to V5 is removed.

rows.subject: STARFlow
rows.size_stated: Model size varied; individual sizes not stated in the text accompanying the figure.
rows.operation_detail: Varied deep-block depth/model size and tracked FID over training.
rows.note: The text says deeper models converge faster and achieve better final performance. FID is not a loss measure for the power-law version.
rows.check: FID is an image sample-quality metric, not a loss scaling law, and its values are figure-only. The 'observed' state has no version to refer to, so it is set to cannot_determine.
